identity.realm: the first spirit gate, where the sea beneath him changed depth from shallow to deep

appearance.presentation: A broad, unhurried man with the patience of a body that has never once been in a hurry, because a deepsalt has never had anywhere to be. He carries himself with the deliberate economy of somebody who knows exactly how much of any substance he is allowed, and he is the only person on the basin floor who looks comfortable lying down.
appearance.age: Sixty-one. Late for a subspecies whose infants are brittle until the second year and whose whole population has never been large enough to need a calendar.
appearance.build: Dense and wide rather than tall, with the extra mass of a body built for a saturated floor instead of for travel. The brine sac shows as a long flat shelf of hardened salt running the length of his upper back and over both shoulder blades, thicker than the parent's by most of a hand, and broad splayed feet pressed flat and permanently splayed wider than a boot.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and dry everywhere above the waterline, with a fine white bloom of dermal crust across the shoulders, throat and jaw that has the look of frost on a window and never comes off. Below the waterline the same skin is slack and faintly translucent.
appearance.hair: Short, coarse and permanently damp at the ends, cropped close because there is nothing on the floor to cut it with and a hair that hangs is a hair that holds brine and crust. He cuts it with a flake off the precipitate and considers the result adequate.
appearance.eyes: Pale, narrow, and habitually half-closed, because his discrimination sharpens the instant his head goes under and dulls by degrees in open air. The habit has trained his face into an expression that strangers read as sleepiness and that is actually an ongoing loss of acuity.
appearance.palette: Wet mineral grey-green and bleached salt-white, with one dark note for the standing brine itself and a single warm ochre kept back for the light that comes through the water. The palette is a waterline: everything above it is chalk, everything below it is the room.
appearance.attire: A sleeveless belted smock of salt-stiffened canvas worn wet to the waist and dry above it, over a long wrap that stays clear of the sac. Broad leather wrist cuffs that seal when submerged and are stiff with bloom within the hour above it. Boots soled for cracked pan, worn through at the toe.
appearance.marks: Dermal crust from the collarbone to the shoulder blades; a pale raised ridge along the sac shelf where it meets skin; both forearms mapped with old shallow cuts that healed white because they were taken in brine; and two shallow concave scars at the hairline where he has put his head down on the floor more times than the floor has forgiven.
appearance.bearing: Weight low and even, and a habit of angling his body so the sac shelf never takes a knock. He sits or kneels where others stand, moves in a flat-footed shuffle, and puts his face in the water the way another man puts his hand on a door.

canon.role_in_story: The whole art of his path asks a practitioner to turn inward and read whatever is standing there, and Sabeth's interior is the best-made thing on the basin floor: a saltfolk soul seated a shade lower than the parent's because the sac is larger, legible to any office with the manners to look at him and durable in a way nobody has ever had the chance to test twice. What nobody at the floor has put together is where that seat sits. It is below the brine. His salt head dulls by degrees in dry air, so the discrimination his entire discipline runs on sharpens the instant his face goes under, and the posture every school on the tier teaches — the sitter rises first, then reads, on the reasoning that a settled practitioner is a readable one — cannot be performed by a body whose instrument is only honest while submerged. He practises the whole ladder of the mind path head-down in the element that is killing him by inches, in the one direction his body runs at all. There is no second deepsalt population and the record does not expect one to arrive, so nothing he learns in that water has anybody to hand it to: no heir, no second reader, no auditor, and no way to tell whether the interior he reads at first light is his own or the precipitate settling over it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the lip of the standing brine with his face down and his back humped under the sac shelf, one palm flat on the precipitate for balance, holding a sitting posture that any school on the tier would call wrong; and when the floor clerk asked whether he had come up for air he lifted one hand clear of the water without breaking the posture, which is the answer she wrote down.
canon.lore: A deepsalt is the saltfolk of one evaporite basin floor, specialised past the parent body until the brine stops being a habitat and becomes a requirement, and the record is blunt about the consequence: taken above the line, a deepsalt does not fall ill, it stops. There is one population, on one floor, and there is not going to be a second one, which makes every fact about the subspecies a fact about a single body and makes anything learned on that floor untransferable by construction rather than by neglect. The saltfolk plan is a plan for drinking brine no softer body could take: extraordinary renal mass, a brine sac laid dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine, a hardened dermal crust, flat grinding teeth and broad feet for cracked pan. The deepsalt has all of it turned up and mobility turned down — a deeper sac, a denser crust, slower tissue turnover, a narrower usable range of sense — and a diet of basin-floor precipitate alone, because the pan organisms the parent eats are above its tolerance. The mind path is open to them, and the record qualifies that openness twice: the salt head dulls fine discrimination in dry air, and the range narrows further than the parent's. So the whole of his craft is a trade. Every sharpening of the instrument costs the instrument. He reads better than anyone else on the floor and reads worse the longer he stays out of the water, and the floor's own weather reports are the only place in his life where that trade is written down as anything other than a private inconvenience. His ascent is bounded by the same wall every saltfolk meets: the sac runs dorsal to the spine and splits the penetrating vessel, so the reservoirs cannot be closed together and the species stops at the eleventh gate whatever it is doing at the time. He did not clear that wall. He cleared the first spirit gate instead, where the sea's own tier changes from shallow to deep and six law seats hold all six groups, so the spatial read his path has been promising finally has something underneath it to push against — and the something underneath it is a floor of brine with a body in it, which is a novelty in this setting and not a convenience. He has never read a standing imprint outside his own water and has never needed to; nothing on the floor would bring one to him, and nothing on the floor is authorised to. What he is therefore the only account of is a body reading itself from underneath, at depth, with no auditor, which is the finding nobody can check and the reason he cannot be made to stop.
history: Born on the saturated floor of a single evaporite basin, into the one population the record has no second sample of, which meant the schooling available to him was whatever his own kin invented and he has been extending that curriculum alone ever since.

Learned early that his discrimination and the air were in opposition, and made the discovery private rather than public, because a child who reports that he reads worse out of water is a child whose family has understood something about the salt head and has no reason to say it aloud.

Began the seated practice face-down in the brine on the reasoning that the posture could not be done any other way, and found that at depth his interior resolved in a way it had never resolved above the line.
Held the first spirit gate at the floor's own standing brine, where six seats hold all six groups and the sea changes depth, and was the first body on the floor ever to make that passage under water.

Refused, on the grounds that nobody could check the refusal, to teach the inverted sitting to anyone else, and has been the sole practitioner of his school of one since the day he made that argument and could not disprove it.

personality.summary: A patient, unhurried man whose entire practice is the inversion of the posture his path teaches: he reads from underneath, in the element that is killing him, because the element is the only place his instrument is sharp. He is entirely without vanity about this and entirely immovable on it.

personality.voice: Low, unhurried and completely level, with the flat precision of a man who has had a great deal of time to choose a small number of words. He does not raise his voice to be heard and he does not lower it to be agreed with. When he refuses something he states the reason first and the refusal second, so that the refusal arrives already understood.

reference_stats.summary: He does not fight in the sense anybody means. He holds a gate open the way his water holds a body up, by being in the element the gate is made of, and an opponent who wants a conversation has to come down into it. What he cannot do is be anywhere else.
strengths: A read that no other body on the floor can sharpen, because his is the only one that improves when submerged.
Total patience, which reads as composure and functions as endurance in a discipline measured in how long one thing can be held.
An interior of unusual durability and unusual legibility, which makes him nearly impossible to deceive about his own state.
Nothing to invade: the seat is below the water and there is no resident up here to occupy.
weaknesses: Entirely immobile above the waterline, and not briefly: a few hours is a serious proposition and a day is a death.
The one discipline he has is the one discipline he cannot pass on, so his school has one member and will have one member.
Blind in dry air in a way that gets worse the longer he is out of it, which is exactly when anybody would want him to be watching.
No independent check on anything he has ever concluded, and he knows it, and has stopped pretending otherwise.
reference_stats.combat_read: He is nearly unkillable inside the brine and cannot be made to leave it, which means any fight with him is a fight conducted on his ground by people who cannot breathe it. Against an opponent who has to surface he has the whole exchange; against one who can wait out his body he has minutes, and he knows the count. He will not be drawn up, so being drawn up is not a tactic available to anybody.
reference_stats.notes: No mechanical rule is claimed here beyond what the bible states. The pairing that matters is anatomical and it is one organ: the sac that seats his soul below the line is the same sac that splits the penetrating vessel and puts a wall at the eleventh gate, so the thing that gives his craft its edge and the thing that stops his ascent are one structure. The bladder named on the body's meridian list is a bookkeeping vessel and is not the same thing as a rung on a ladder; nothing here conflates the two.

art.palette_notes: Everything above the water is chalk and everything below it is the room, and the palette is split at that line so that no shot has to choose which side of him is the real one. The one warm ochre is reserved for light coming up through the brine, so that warmth in frame always means submerged, and the accent is spent only on the interior of the shot.

identity.realm: the gate where clarity and purity stop agreeing, which is the gate her body prices

appearance.presentation: A tall, angular woman who looks expensive and unwell in the same glance, because dryness and refinement arrive on her together. She carries herself with the rigid precision of somebody managing a quantity, and there is a distinct pause before anything wet happens near her.
appearance.age: Fifty-three. Long past the point where the basin would have expected a saltfolk of her kind to be anything but a reader.
appearance.build: Broad through the shoulders and long in the forearm, with extraordinary renal mass showing as a width across the middle back and a brine sac lying as a long hardened ridge under the shoulder blades. Broad splayed feet, flat grinding teeth, and a frame that looks heavier than it is because the sac reads as load.
appearance.complexion: Chalk-white and tight above the shoulders where the air has been drying her, with the dermal crust a fine hard grey bloom along the jaw and the forearms. She has started to keep her sleeves down over the worst of it, which she attributes to glare.
appearance.hair: Bleached to the colour of old bone and drawn back hard, kept oiled with something the pan produces, because hair that is not protected is hair that the crust takes within the week. It is the only part of her she spends attention on.
appearance.eyes: Pale, reddened at the inner corner, and no longer narrowing in dry air. They hold their sharpness open in air that would put a softer body's eyes to water, and that is the entire subject of her life.
appearance.palette: Bleached white, hard grey-blue and the particular flat glare of dry ground, with the saturated mineral green of standing brine kept as the only cool colour and used sparingly. One warm ochre for the light she is walking toward.
appearance.attire: A long belted coat of undyed salt-stiffened canvas, high-collared, closed to the throat even in the heat, with long sleeves and stiffened cuffs. Beneath it a close linen wrap and a second pair of trousers for the walk. Boots soled for cracked pan, resoled twice since she left the water.
appearance.marks: Dermal crust along the jaw and both forearms; the pale ridge of the sac across the upper back; chapping at the knuckles that will not close; and, since she began walking, a permanent fine haze of white on everything she owns.
appearance.bearing: Upright and very straight, shoulders square, walking with the deliberate placement of somebody who has counted how far it is to the next water and is spending that count carefully. She never stands with her back to a wall of open ground, and she has begun to flinch at the word rain.

canon.role_in_story: Every saltfolk is a body that concentrates brine past the point at which ordinary water poisons, which is the whole of what lets it live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back — and the price is total. Carried onto fresher ground a saltfolk is already dying, fails above the line within about nine days, and is caught out in rain the way a softer body is caught in a fall. Ilmira has found the third thing about that body, which is not in the record's summary of the species and which she found by accident and has not been able to give away: the salt head dulls fine discrimination in dry air, so the drier the ground she stands on, the finer the read. Her craft and her life run in opposite directions on the same axis. The band her path is climbing asks for clarity and purity to stop agreeing with each other and to be held apart, and the way to hold them apart is precisely to come out of the water — so the discipline that the immortal tier demands of her is a discipline of standing in the one place her body cannot survive, a little further up, every season, than the season before. She is not doing this for a reason anybody in the basin would recognise as a reason. She is doing it because a practice that sharpens as you leave is a practice that can be measured, and hers cannot be measured any other way, and the basin's best readers cannot measure anything at all in dry air. The dominion's depth-books still list her as resident because nobody has ever gone up a shelf and come back off the books. Her advantage and her ruin are the same organ: the extraordinary renal mass that lets her concentrate four orders of dilution is the thing that has been failing since she stopped drinking at saturation, and the taste she is trading her life for is the taste those kidneys make.
canon.first_appearance: First seen halfway up a drying shelf above the last standing brine with her coat closed to the throat and one hand shading her eyes from glare that was never a problem for her before, pausing to put two fingers into a damp patch of crust and then looking at them for a while before saying the ground is better here than it was.
canon.lore: A saltfolk is a people built for brine no softer body could drink. Their kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, which lets them occupy ground where the supply never fails and everything else dies back, and the same arrangement makes them the least mobile people in the setting: they need a standing brine supply within a day of travel, a saltfolk on fresh ground is a body already failing, and there is no cultivation that repairs any of it. Their frame answers for that with extraordinary renal mass, a brine sac laid dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine, a hardened dermal crust, flat grinding teeth and broad splayed feet for ground that cracks. They read brine concentration across four orders of dilution where a human nose finds only sour, which makes them the best chemical sense in the record and makes their vision no better than anything else's and poor in glare. Their mind path is open, and the qualification the record attaches to that openness is the entire content of her life: the salt head dulls fine discrimination in dry air. It is a small clause and it does two things at once. It makes the path harder for her than for anyone else at ground level, and it makes her sharper than anyone else anywhere above it, because the dullness is a function of the medium rather than of the instrument. Her basin understood that clause exactly once, early, in the sense that it understood it and decided there was no reason to act on it. She has been acting on it for years. What she is climbing toward is a band that asks for clarity and purity to be held apart, which is the first place on her ladder where the two requirements genuinely diverge, and the divergence is a physical fact about a body that has to be in air to achieve it. Every shelf she takes is a shelf where her readings get finer and where the walk back down to water gets longer. The death that ends this is not dramatic and is not a gate refusing her; it is a pair of kidneys that have been concentrating salt for a body that no longer supplies it, which is the ordinary price of her species and the reason no cultivation repairs it. She has written the sequence down in a schoolbook she bought second-hand and carries it to nobody, because the basin has no second saltfolk reader and she cannot be checked and does not want to be.
history: Born on the pan above geography.exhausted_seam, into a family whose standing was a depth at which they were permitted to moor, and raised on the understanding that the standing was the inheritance and the body was the container for it.

Learned the brine line by taste before she could read a figure, which is the ordinary education of her species and which left her with a discrimination she could not explain to anyone who had not been raised the same way.
Noticed as an adolescent that the readings sharpened when she had been out in the dry, and told one person, and was told not to make a story out of a private peculiarity.

Held a mind gate while standing on ground her body could not keep, and found the practice legible where the same practice had been nearly impossible at the water, and understood that the two facts were one fact.
Began leaving the saturation line a season at a time, and has taught, in the pan's two schools, that the seated posture is something one does while one can still drink.

reference_stats.summary: She fights by being somewhere her opponent cannot follow for long and by reading faster than they can move, and both advantages have a shelf under them. She will not be drawn down to the water, because the water is the one place her craft is blunt, and that refusal is the whole of her tactical situation.
strengths: A chemical sense that reads four orders of dilution, and which is sharper, not blunter, the drier the ground — the exact inverse of the species norm.
Discipline sustained under worsening conditions without any change of method.
Extraordinary renal mass, which makes her nearly immune to what a drier body would be poisoned by.
An absolute, stated and non-negotiable knowledge of her own position on the ground, kept current without being asked.
weaknesses: Total dependence on the brine supply, with the walk back to it growing every season she does not return.
A full, thick coat and a slow frame; she cannot disengage quickly on ground that is not her own.
Rain, which for her species is a drowning condition rather than weather.
No reader on her shelf. There is nobody on a drying shelf who can check a figure she has taken in dry air, and there never will be.
reference_stats.combat_read: She wants high ground and she wants to stay on it, and the second want is the one that kills her. Against anything that has to close she has the read and the range; against anything patient she has a body whose supply is measured in walking distance and whose advantage improves precisely as that supply shortens. She cannot be made to go back down, which makes her very hard to corner and very easy to wait for.

appearance.presentation: A tall, quiet, under-described figure whose shape is partly a property of what they are standing on. They hold themselves arranged along an edge rather than centred on it, and a viewer who changes the viewer's own angle changes their outline. Nothing about them is symmetrical for long.
appearance.age: No age. The record says this population was not born and is not descended, and that what looks like a population may be one very old thing wearing a lot of faces.
appearance.build: Arranged rather than assembled, taking its shape from whatever inner surface it stands against, and described in the record as unsettled and under-described. Long, still, thin at the places where a body would be thickest and set at odd angles at the joints, as though the frame were still being negotiated.
appearance.complexion: Pale mineral grey with a faint luminous cast that does not come from any light in the room and cannot be pointed at a source. Where they have stood long enough it is polished; where they have just moved it is not.
appearance.hair: None, or the nearest local equivalent: a fine dark mineral deposit along one temple that reads as hair and shifts length between portraits, which the record attributes to the shape being taken from the surface.
appearance.eyes: Wide, still and dark, with the particular unblinking attention of somebody hearing the room rather than looking at it. They do not track a face across a room; they track the seam the room is built along.
appearance.palette: Sealed stone grey, warm resin amber where the resonance is audible, and a single cold metal note for the object's own pitch. Nothing saturated anywhere, because nothing in this body is stored.
appearance.attire: A close unseamed covering of grey canvas that follows the surface beneath rather than the body above it, high at the collar, long at the sleeve, belted once at the waist with a length that lets them hang from a wall as easily as stand. Bare, splayed, rock-gloved hands.
appearance.marks: A resonance bloom across the sternum and both forearms, dark at the edges; a hairline seam at the jaw where the shape is being negotiated; and the amber cast strongest at the left palm, which is the hand that rests on the seal.
appearance.bearing: Still to a degree that reads as attention rather than calm, angled to a wall or a seam in nearly every frame, and turning the head toward sounds rather than toward people. They never stand in the centre of a room.

canon.role_in_story: Everything the mind path is built to do, Oriven does on somebody else's schedule. A vaultborn's qi comes from exactly one resonator — the object they were sealed inside, held under a charter and described only by people who are already answering it — and a single source means the seventeenth gate, the first that needs two flank vessels pressurised at the same time, is not a wall for them but a cycle. It opens when the object's resonance peaks and it shuts when it does not, and because their soul is seated along the resonance path and distributed through the seal rather than held in a body, there is no interior that belongs to them for the depth to be held in. That is the whole of what nobody outside has worked out about them: their deepest attainment is legible from the corridor. Any office that knows when the seal peaks knows what Oriven can hold that week, and can price it, schedule against it, and refuse it, and none of that requires knowing anything about Oriven. The cost is on the same organ as the advantage and it is total. The body has exactly one supply and no redundancy whatsoever, so there is no version of this species that survives being carried out of the seal, and no technique, item or realm in the record that changes that. The discipline the path is named for costs them nothing and means nothing either, because a soul distributed through an object empties and fills with the object rather than on command. And nobody inside has ever agreed on a measurement: the record says outright that no one who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements, which means the one figure that would price Oriven correctly has never existed.
canon.first_appearance: First seen with the left palm flat against a seam in the seal's inner wall, standing at an angle to the room rather than in it, head turned toward a vibration no one else in the corridor can hear, and answering a question about their progress by holding up one finger and then, after a pause long enough to be worth writing down, adding a second.
canon.lore: A vaultborn is not born and is not descended. A population was sealed inside an authored object and has been answering that object's resonance ever since, and their qi comes from it, which is why they hold the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flank vessels — not because the vessels are hard but because the supply is single and one resonator can pressurise one flank or the other and never both. That single fact organises the entire species, and it organises this body in a way the rest of the record has only begun to notice. The mind path is the one discipline in the setting that asks a practitioner to hold, and Oriven's holding is the object's holding: their qi is seated along the resonance path, distributed through the seal, so the act of settling is not something they do but something the object does at them. The seventeenth gate is the first that requires two flank vessels pressurised at once, which for this body is not a threshold crossed once but a window that opens on the object's cycle and closes on it again, and the band above asks for a will held steadily rather than a sea filled — which is the one request a single-source body cannot answer in any season, let alone on any schedule. So the deepest thing Oriven can do is also the most legible thing about them. There is an office in the setting that would price it, and the office does not need to meet them; it needs to know the object's cycle, and the cycle is not a secret because the object makes a sound and everybody inside can hear it. What makes this worse than a plain exposure is that the species itself is unsettled and under-described in the record: their anatomy is unsettled, they take their shape from whatever they are standing on, and no one who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements. So Oriven is not merely public; they are public in a currency nobody has managed to mint. Every claim about what this body can do is a claim about one respondent, taken once, at a different hour, in a different position, against a different surface. The resonator itself is held under an extraction guild's charter and is described only by those already answering it, which means the description and the described are the same population. There is a grief in that which the setting has not named: a body whose only teacher is the thing that supplies it, whose only reader is itself, and whose one sound is a pitch that everybody can hear and nobody can measure.
history: Not born into the seal and not descended into it; present inside the object from the earliest point any inside record can name, with no date for that point and no parent named by anybody.
Learned the object's pitch before language, which is the ordinary education of this species and the reason their speech is sparse and precise and mostly about timing.
Found that the deepest gate on their ladder opens and shuts with the object's cycle rather than with any effort of their own, and understood immediately that this made them legible from outside.
Attempted, once, to hold the gate through a cycle in which the object did not support it, and established the species' ceiling as a property of supply rather than of body.
Began answering questions about their attainment only in terms of the cycle, on the reasoning that any other answer would be an absolute figure produced by a body nobody has measured twice.

personality.summary: A still, careful, unsentimental figure who speaks in timings and has stopped pretending to have an interior that belongs to them alone. They are not haunted by the arrangement; they have simply reorganised everything around it, and the unsettling thing about them is the tidiness.
traits: exact about timing
unattached to status
patient past the point of endurance
literal-minded to a fault
quietly protective of anybody who is measuring them
mannerisms: stands against a seam rather than in the middle of a room
turns the head to vibration rather than to voice
answers with a hand held up before any words
counts a silence aloud rather than filling it
washes the left palm, always the left, before touching anything
motivations: to be measured properly once
to hear the object answered by somebody other than themselves
to find out what they are when the seal is not sounding
to keep the one accurate thing they know accurate
flaws: has organised themselves entirely around a supply they did not choose and calls that a discipline
cannot distinguish their own resolution from the object's resonance
will not answer a direct question when a timed one is available
has never left and has formed opinions about leaving that no experience informs
personality.voice: Few words, placed rather than spoken, with long pauses that are not hesitation but measurement. They do not repeat themselves and they do not explain twice. The register is flat and unornamented and occasionally takes several seconds to arrive, and when it does arrive it is exact.
taboos: will not be weighed, seated, counted or timed by anybody as a demonstration
will not accept a reading taken during a cycle their own body cannot account for
will not touch the seal's outer face while the extraction guild's charter is in force
will not be described as a population, and will correct it

the last immortal-band gate, which is the one place their path is already reading spatial the way the top tier does

reference_stats.summary: They do not choose ground; they choose a seam. Everything they do happens within the object's cycle, which means they can be posted anywhere the seal reaches and are worth exactly what the seal is worth at that hour. What beats them is anything that ignores the cycle and simply keeps coming.
strengths: Depth that is not theirs to lose and therefore cannot be contested on the day it is held.
An interior distributed rather than seated, which is very hard to invade and very hard to locate.
A tolerance for waiting without discomfort that no store-bodied practitioner here matches.
Total alertness to the object, and through it to the room, at a resolution nobody outside can reproduce.
weaknesses: One supply and no redundancy of any kind, so the entire discipline has a single point of failure and the body shares it.
Nothing to show for any attainment except the hour it happened, and every hour can be re-read by a stranger.
Under-described by the record itself, so the account of their own capability is not reliable in either direction.
Wholly non-portable: there is no version of this that leaves the object and continues.
reference_stats.combat_read: Read the cycle before the fight and the fight is already decided, because their ceiling arrives and departs on the object's schedule and any opponent who knows the pitch can time it. Read it wrong and they are simply unavailable, in the specific way that a single-source body is unavailable: not weakened, not slowed, absent. They will not be pressed, and pressing costs the seal.
reference_stats.notes: No mechanical rule is claimed beyond the bible, and the two fields the brief warns about are kept apart here: this record's ladder is fully open, because the species closes only the body path, and its published ceiling of zero means unbounded rather than absent. There is no ladder question in this character at all. The pairing is anatomical and it is one supply: the resonance that makes their depth possible is the same single source that means the object cannot be left, so the advantage and the ruin are the same object and neither can be traded for the other. The bladder on the body's meridian list is a bookkeeping vessel of another path and is not a rung on this one.

appearance.presentation: A lean, watchful man with the frame of somebody built to be nowhere in particular and to be looking at something constantly. He is pre-eminently still and it reads as attention, and the eyes do most of the work the rest of the body declines.
appearance.age: A hundred and eighty-something and entirely unbothered by it, because the record puts a tidecaller's lifespan alongside the longest-lived bodies here and this one has never once spent it on a plan.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and deep-chested, with a long neck and hands that are made for holding a line of sight rather than a weight. Nothing on him is arranged for being struck and he wears it without apology.
appearance.complexion: Cool, faintly translucent at the cheek and temple in cold light, with the damp look of somebody who has been in weather rather than near it.
appearance.hair: Dark, straight and cut once a year to the same length by the same hand, because a tidecaller has water affinity and no other affinity and the sea does the rest of the work on it.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set, grey, and of a fix that people find uncomfortable because it arrives before they have decided to be looked at. The single feature he has ever been described as beautiful, and he has no use for it.
appearance.palette: Cold sea grey and wet slate, with one bleached bone-white at the collar and a single deep tide-green reserved for water he is currently reading.
appearance.attire: A high-collared long coat of grey-blue oilskin worn to the throat and belted once, over a close knit beneath; sleeves long and buttoned at the wrist; sea boots worn low at the heel because a body built for looking is not a body for standing still on.
appearance.marks: Salt-line scarring at the cuffs where the coat has dried at the seam more times than the seam likes; a pale cord-mark at the left wrist from a gauge line held too long in one position; and the eyes, which are the only thing about him anybody looks at twice.
appearance.bearing: Never quite square to anything and never quite still. He angles to a sightline, holds a look rather than a stance, and puts himself at the edge of a group rather than the centre of it, without any apparent awareness that he is doing it.

canon.role_in_story: A tidecaller was assembled for looking rather than for being hit, and the record gives its body a ceiling of zero with no mechanism attached at all — which is the difference that matters, because a zero there is not an absence of a ladder, it is a ladder with nothing standing on the last step. Everything except the body path is open to him. What follows from that is the only real content of his position in the setting: nothing has ever refused Corvane, and nothing has ever told him where the edge is either. Every other practitioner here can name the gate ahead of them and work toward it, and can be certified against a known figure. He has no figure and no gate, and the mind path's founding act — turn inward and find the limit of what you are — returns him nothing, because the boundary was never drawn on him in the first place. So he does the only thing left, which is to be the one who goes past whatever the record has finished saying, and to come back with something, and he has been doing it for well over a century and the something has never been publishable. The advantage and its cost are the same body. His frame cannot be hit, which makes him immune to the answer the setting uses on anything that goes too far: there is no confrontation available, so the entire apparatus that tests an unbounded practitioner has nothing to grip. And the coast, which has spent four generations arranging itself so that no single body is one, has ended up with precisely that in him anyway, because a man who reads better than anyone on either shore is a single point of failure no matter what he is willing to do about it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the tideline with his feet in the water and his coat already soaked to the second button, holding one unbroken look out across the water for so long that a delegate asked him twice what he was reading, and giving the same answer both times: nothing in particular, and more than usual today.
canon.lore: A tidecaller is a race rather than a species and it is built for a single purpose. It is long-lived, comprehension and will carry it through realms that would end a hotter body, it holds water affinity and nothing else, and it cannot take the body path at all, because it was assembled for looking rather than for being hit. Those are the authored facts and they are not many. What is not authored is the ceiling, and this is the part that undoes most of what people assume about him: his record carries a ceiling of zero, which in this setting's arithmetic means unbounded, and it carries no mechanism whatsoever, unlike almost every other body in the file. There is no gate standing in his way and no gate standing behind him either. The ladder is real — his path is wide open, and everything a practitioner can do he can attempt — but there is no published point at which it stops, so he is the only mind-path body here for whom the question of his limit has no answer that anybody else is responsible for. That is the whole of his difficulty and it is not a small one, because the discipline he is trained in begins by turning attention inward and reading the boundary of the self. He does that. He gets a very clear account of a very well-made interior, and it contains no edge. Practitioners all over the setting are being graded against a figure; he is being sent past the end of the written material to find out what is there, and what he finds is not a wall but a widening he cannot certify, which is worse in one specific way and better in none that he has found. The frame that makes him good at this is the frame that makes him untouchable: there is no confrontation to be had with a body that was not built to take a blow, so the mechanism this setting uses on anything that goes further than expected is unavailable to him by construction. Two institutions want that mechanism and neither can have it. One seats a law and reads what the frame newly permits, and cannot seat anything for a body that has never stopped permitting. The other teaches that a slot spent on an absence is money spent on nothing, and his own ceiling is an absence in the file — a zero that cannot be told apart from a question nobody asked. He would settle it himself in an afternoon if there were anyone on either shore with a body built to check him.
history: Born on the leeward coast of the Cloudshelf with a tidecaller's long sight and a family that had already accepted it as a profession rather than a gift, since a thing built for looking does not have to be talked into looking.

Found out at a young age that his record's ceiling was a zero with nothing written under it, and asked the office that keeps the file, and was told the file was not wrong and that nobody had a reason to write a reason.
Learned the confederacy's rules about not being a single point of failure at the same time he discovered he was one, and has been the specific, awkward answer to that rule for over a century.
Went past the last realm anybody on his coast has an account of, and came back able to describe what was there and unable to show that the description was of anything rather than of him.
Stopped competing for posts that a body of his construction cannot hold, and started being sent, which is the arrangement everybody now relies on and nobody has ever priced.

personality.summary: An unhurried, watchful, quietly frustrated man whose entire difficulty is that nothing in the record has ever stopped him. He is not vain about it and not modest either; he is precise, which is the only honest response to a body with no published end.

reference_stats.summary: He wins by never being where the fight is, and the reason he cannot simply win is that the whole coast now depends on a single reading and he is the one who takes it. He is difficult to threaten and easy to obstruct, because an obstruction only has to be placed between him and the water.
strengths: A read that holds unbroken across a tide change and a night, which no body on either shore has matched.
A frame that cannot be usefully struck, which makes most forms of pressure simply not apply.
Comprehension and will carrying him through realms a hotter body would not survive.
Patience at a scale that lets him wait out an opponent who has to eat.
weaknesses: A single point of failure in a league whose founding rule is that there must not be one.
No frame for the confrontation this setting uses to answer anything that goes too far, so no test of him is available to anybody.
No certifiable account of his own reach, which makes every claim about him a rumour with a competent man attached.
Water affinity and no other, so he is worth very little anywhere the water is not.
reference_stats.combat_read: He is not going to be fought, because he will not be reached and will not close, and anyone who chases him across open ground has simply spent the tide. What beats him is arithmetic rather than force: put something between him and the water, or wait for the water to move on without him, or simply ask him a question at the wrong hour. He has never been hit and he does not think about being hit, which is a real gap.
reference_stats.notes: No mechanical rule is claimed beyond the bible, and the two fields that are easy to conflate are kept explicitly apart here: the ceiling of zero on this body's record means unbounded, not the absence of a ladder, and the ladder question is answered by the closed-paths field, which for this species closes the body path only. Everything above assumes that reading. The pairing here is anatomical and it is one frame: the same build that cannot be struck is the build that cannot be tested, so his immunity and his uncertifiability are the same structure. The bladder named among the body's meridians is a bookkeeping vessel of the body's own path and is not a rung on this ladder.

identity.realm: the first immortal gate, where a self must be held apart from more than one region at once

appearance.presentation: A broad, unhurried, immensely patient woman with the heaviness of a body built to store and the stillness of one that does most of its work asleep. She looks like the weather and behaves like the calendar, and the impression is accurate in both cases.
appearance.age: Ninety. The record puts a longwinter's lifespan alongside the longest bodies in the setting, and she has spent almost none of the difference on a plan.
appearance.build: Broad and low, heavy with subcutaneous fat, with reduced limb length and a lowered cold-tolerant core. The frame is built to hold a winter and does so visibly; there is nothing spare on it and nothing delicate.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly waxy, chapped at the hands and permanently a little flushed across the cheeks in cold air, the way her kind is flushed when the core is up.
appearance.hair: Pale brown going grey at the temples, worn in a single low plait that she re-braids on waking and does not think about again, which for a body that is awake for a few weeks a year is most of its grooming.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and steady, with the wide quiet attention of a creature that can wait out almost anything and has had a great deal of practice. She looks at people as though she intends to still be looking at them next season.
appearance.palette: Cold bone, undyed wool brown and the blue-white of standing snow, with one warm lamp ochre kept strictly for the indoors and the short waking hours.
appearance.attire: Layered undyed hide and wool in the plains manner, patched at the shoulder and heavy at the hem, over felted boots soled for packed snow. A long unseamed wrap that goes on over everything and comes off over everything, because dressing a longwinter is a decision about the season.
appearance.marks: Chapping across both hands, a burn scar at the inside of one wrist where a lamp was knocked over during a short waking, and the deep-set pallor at the temples that her kind wears in the cold months.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried to the point of geological, economical with movement, and completely unbothered by any small emergency. She sits down before she is tired and stands up before she is stiff, and every choice she makes is on a scale of weeks rather than hours.

canon.role_in_story: The founding move of the whole mind path is subtraction: empty the head, spend nothing, keep nothing, and the discipline is priced in how well a body can hold still with a charge in it and then let it go. Solvay's body does the opposite on every axis and does it without her. A longwinter carries a winter as fat rather than as qi, the same cycle that stores fat stores qi, the turnover is slow enough that breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, and the soul is held very deep and very quiet, which is why it is so hard to read and so hard to damage. Put those facts beside the path's founding move and you get her entire life: every sitting she ends with more in her than she began with. Her clarity rises whether she works or not. That is an extraordinary advantage — nothing she has accumulated has ever been lost to a failed gate, and no discipline of deliberate spending has ever been able to demonstrate anything against her — and it is also the reason she is the only practitioner in the setting who cannot prove that anything she holds is hers. The accumulation is bought from the weather. A warm year is a bad year for her kind and a warm decade is a catastrophe, so the one thing she is steadily accumulating is being supplied by a climate she does not control and cannot argue with. And the office in this setting whose entire content is keeping figures in one head that is never permitted to write them down has twice offered her the post and twice withdrawn it, because the practice needs a head that will not be interrupted and hers is asleep for most of the year. Everything Solvay has demonstrated has therefore been kept by somebody else who was not present for it, in a hand that is not hers, and she has never once been in a position to check.
canon.first_appearance: First seen awake on a ridge shelf in the eating weeks, sitting very still with a slate on her knees that she was not writing on, and when asked what she was doing said she was trying to find out whether the sitting had been hers, and that she would know in about nine months.
canon.lore: A longwinter is the cold-climate answer to a survival problem that only has one shape: pack the winter as body fat, and accept that almost nothing about the year is available for anything else. The anatomy follows — a broad low frame, heavy subcutaneous fat, a lowered core temperature that runs for eleven months, reduced limbs, and a species that eats enormously during a few weeks and digests more out of frozen food than anything else in the record does. The mind path is open to them and the record's own description of the species is that it is patient by physiology rather than by discipline, which is a fair sentence until you put it next to what the discipline actually is. The mind path is founded on subtraction. Every office and school in this setting teaches a sitting, and the ladder is priced in what a body can hold perfectly still with a charge held and then let go, and the emptying is the founding move rather than an ornament of it. Solvay's physiology cannot do the emptying. The same cycle that stores fat stores qi, the turnover is a fraction of a body a year, so what she takes in accumulates rather than circulates, and her breakthroughs arrive late and almost never fail, because nothing in that design has a mechanism for losing what it has already got. So her sea fills whether or not she sits, her clarity sharpens on a schedule set by her metabolism rather than by her attention, and she has spent her life unable to separate the two. The cost is not the accumulation, which is a gift beyond anything the discipline promises; it is that the accumulation is bought from the weather. A warm year is a bad year for this species and a warm decade is a catastrophe, which means the supply of her one advantage is a climate she does not own. Everything she has shown has been recorded by other hands, because the setting's one institution that pays a body for keeping figures in its head requires a head that will not be interrupted, and hers spends most of the year not being available to interrupt. Two households have offered her that post and withdrawn it, which is a more honest outcome than either of them managed at the time. She has never disputed it. She has never once been able to check her own work either, and the standing question of her life is whether the clarity she has is a discipline or a climate.
history: Born on a high-latitude slope above geography.sixfold_ridge into a household whose marriages were arranged across the warming houses, on the reasoning that a winter is a shared problem and a store is not.

Learned to read in the short waking months and to sit for the long ones, which is the ordinary education of her species and which meant her first real discipline was a sitting she could not interrupt.

Found out in her twenties that her clarity improved whether she sat or not, and kept the finding to herself for a decade because a practitioner who cannot account for her own progress is not a practitioner anybody can send anywhere.
Was offered the keeper's post by a house that keeps its figures in one unwritten head, and withdrew the offer itself when it realised the post requires a head that will not be interrupted.
Began giving her findings to whoever is present, in a written form with her name on it and no claim attached, on the reasoning that a record she cannot check should at least be attributable.

personality.summary: A vast, slow, unbothered woman who has arrived at the most serious question in her discipline and cannot answer it about herself. She is not modest and not proud; she has simply run out of things to be either about.

unfailingly honest about uncertainty
immovable once she has said a thing
slow to anger and long in keeping it
given to writing things down with her name on them
mannerisms: sits down before she is tired and stands before she is stiff
speaks in seasons rather than hours

wakes slowly and is entirely herself by the second hour
motivations: to find out whether the sitting was hers
to have one thing that can be attributed to her without a witness
to reach a gate before a warm decade comes
to be useful in the weeks she is awake
flaws: cannot distinguish her own discipline from her own metabolism and has stopped trying to argue the point with herself
will not refuse an offer until it has been withdrawn from her
gives away work she cannot check
treats her own enormous reserves as a resource and not as the only evidence against herself
personality.voice: Very low, very slow, and shaped by long silences rather than by emphasis. She begins sentences a long way before she finishes them and does not hurry the end. She is careful with time words in a way people notice and cannot place: she says things in seasons and weather, and it is not a figure of speech, it is the only unit her life runs on.
taboos: will not claim a result she cannot attribute
will not be woken for a reading
will not take a post that requires her to be present year-round
will not eat a meal before the household has, and has gone hungry rather than break the rule

relationships.note: the body that carries a winter as fat rather than as qi, and therefore cannot perform the subtraction its path is founded on
the first immortal gate, where a self has to be held apart from more than one region at once and everything she holds is one undifferentiated reserve
the crust that records fall thickness in its own growth, so a quiet decade is legible on the rock years after the arc stops being interesting

reference_stats.summary: She does not fight at all. She holds, which is the mind path's whole vocabulary, and she holds for eleven months whether or not she intends to. Anything that measures endurance loses. Anything that measures her own work cannot be run at all, because she is asleep when the measurement is taken.
strengths: Reserves that have never once been lost to a failed gate, because nothing in her design can lose what it has already got.
A soul held very deep and very quiet, which makes her exceptionally hard to read and exceptionally hard to damage.
Patience at a scale no store-bodied practitioner here approaches, including her own.
A total immunity to deliberate-spending disciplines, because there is nothing in her for them to spend.
weaknesses: Slow and nearly helpless during torpor, which is most of the year, and cannot be woken quickly.
No way to demonstrate that a single thing she holds is hers, which makes her unpromotable on evidence and unpromotable on anything else.
Wholly dependent on a real winter, and a warm decade would take everything she has at once.
Eleven months of the year in which she is a large, warm, immobile target.
reference_stats.combat_read: Nothing that measures a fight touches her, and nothing that measures a season touches her either. What beats her is a room she is awake in: eleven weeks is not long, and an opponent who knows which eleven weeks can be in the room for all of them. She cannot be hurried and cannot be woken, which makes her extremely hard to defeat and comparatively easy to simply wait out.
reference_stats.notes: No mechanical rule is claimed beyond the bible. The pairing is anatomical and it is one cycle: the physiology that stores fat stores qi, so the same unbroken cycle that gives her an unbroken reserve also makes every gain indistinguishable from the weather that supplied it. The bladder named among the body's meridians is a bookkeeping vessel and is a different axis from a rung on a ladder; nothing here treats the two as the same kind of thing, and nothing here gives her a tier for it.

art.palette_notes: Bone, undyed wool and snow, with the lamp ochre rationed to the indoor frames and the short waking hours, because the warmth in this character is time rather than temperature. Skin and hide read as value and texture, never as colour. Any frame with more light in it than she could possibly use in the eating weeks is a frame of the wrong hour.
